# Zero-Config Frontend Bridge Template

This template creates a strongly typed, zero-dependency client bridge (`src/lib/api-client.ts` or `public/api-client.js`). It allows any frontend (React, Next.js, Vite, Vue, Svelte, or vanilla HTML/JS) to communicate with the generated backend with zero configuration and automated error handling.

---

## 1. TypeScript Production Bridge (`src/lib/api-client.ts`)

```typescript
/**
 * Zero-to-Live API Client Bridge
 * Auto-generated by zero-to-live-api
 */

export interface ApiResponse<T = unknown> {
  success: boolean;
  data?: T;
  error?: {
    code: string;
    message: string;
    details?: unknown;
  };
}

export class ApiClientError extends Error {
  public code: string;
  public status: number;
  public details?: unknown;

  constructor(message: string, code: string, status: number, details?: unknown) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'ApiClientError';
    this.code = code;
    this.status = status;
    this.details = details;
  }
}

// Environment Base URL Resolver
function getBaseUrl(): string {
  // Vite environment
  if (typeof import.meta !== 'undefined' && (import.meta as any).env?.VITE_API_URL) {
    return (import.meta as any).env.VITE_API_URL;
  }
  // Next.js environment
  if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env?.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL) {
    return process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL;
  }
  // Browser window context
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.location.origin) {
    return window.location.origin;
  }
  // Default fallback
  return 'http://127.0.0.1:3000';
}

const BASE_URL = getBaseUrl();

async function request<T>(path: string, options: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
  const url = `${BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '')}/${path.replace(/^\//, '')}`;
  
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers || {});
  if (!headers.has('Content-Type') && options.body) {
    headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  }

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    ...options,
    headers,
  });

  let payload: ApiResponse<T>;
  try {
    payload = await response.json();
  } catch {
    throw new ApiClientError(
      `Failed to parse server response from ${path}`,
      'PARSE_ERROR',
      response.status
    );
  }

  if (!response.ok || payload.success === false) {
    const errorInfo = payload.error || {
      code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR',
      message: response.statusText || 'Request failed',
    };
    throw new ApiClientError(
      errorInfo.message,
      errorInfo.code,
      response.status,
      errorInfo.details
    );
  }

  return payload.data as T;
}

// Concrete API Method Handlers
export const api = {
  // System Health
  health: {
    check: () => request<{ status: string; timestamp: string }>('/health'),
  },

  // Resource Methods (Tailored to user entity, e.g. leads)
  records: {
    list: (category?: string) => {
      const query = category ? `?category=${encodeURIComponent(category)}` : '';
      return request<any[]>(`/api/records${query}`, { method: 'GET' });
    },
    create: (data: Record<string, unknown>) => {
      return request<any>('/api/records', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify(data),
      });
    },
  },
};

export default api;
```

## 2. 1-Line Frontend Usage Examples

### In a React / Next.js Component:
```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { api, ApiClientError } from '@/lib/api-client';

export function ContactForm() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<string | null>(null);

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    setLoading(true);
    setStatus(null);

    const formData = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
    const payload = Object.fromEntries(formData.entries());

    try {
      // ONE LINE EXECUTION:
      const result = await api.records.create(payload);
      setStatus(`Saved successfully with ID: ${result.id}`);
      e.currentTarget.reset();
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof ApiClientError) {
        setStatus(`Error: ${err.message} (${err.code})`);
      } else {
        setStatus('An unexpected error occurred.');
      }
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="space-y-4">
      <input name="title" placeholder="Title" required className="border p-2 rounded" />
      <button type="submit" disabled={loading} className="bg-blue-600 text-white px-4 py-2 rounded">
        {loading ? 'Saving...' : 'Submit'}
      </button>
      {status && <p className="text-sm">{status}</p>}
    </form>
  );
}
```

## 3. Vanilla JavaScript Version (`public/api-client.js`)

```javascript
(function (root, factory) {
  root.api = factory();
})(typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window : this, function () {
  const BASE_URL = window.location.origin || 'http://127.0.0.1:3000';

  async function request(path, options = {}) {
    const url = `${BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '')}/${path.replace(/^\//, '')}`;
    const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(options.headers || {}) };

    const res = await fetch(url, { ...options, headers });
    const json = await res.json();

    if (!res.ok || json.success === false) {
      const err = json.error || { message: 'Request failed', code: 'API_ERROR' };
      throw new Error(`[${err.code}] ${err.message}`);
    }
    return json.data;
  }

  return {
    records: {
      list: () => request('/api/records'),
      create: (data) => request('/api/records', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) }),
    },
  };
});
```
